> **Third measurement of this, and the wording changed for the worse.** 70% of off-case answers were
> unsupported at first; telling the patient the fact list is not a summary and giving it the exact words
> to use brought that to 55%; turning the ban on answering "no" into a reason and a consequence took it
> back to the 65% below. Worse in kind as well: instead of a bare "No." the model began decorating the
> denial ("No chest pain. Just this stubborn cough.", "My wife's fine, kids are grown and live
> elsewhere"), and the grader labelled that second one "not sure" when it is an invented family history.
>
> Twenty graded answers over ten questions cannot separate variants two or three answers apart, so
> every one of those three numbers is inside the noise of the others. Read this as "the prompt does not
> hold this line", which all three agree on, and not as a ranking. The next step is a judge that can say
> whether a question was about the person's situation at all, so the engine can enforce the answer
> instead of asking for it; see src/offCase.ts.
